person: Nadia Haddad is a 50-year-old part-time bookkeeper who can sit at a screen for about twenty minutes before her spine pain forces a break. Her household is her, her husband Joseph and their 17-year-old son Karim, plus her father Elias, who lives in the back apartment and files his own taxes. This year the family got bills from Saint Ardent for her ER visit and spinal injection and for Karim's wrist X-ray, and a collection agency has now written. She does not trust forms that time out, wants to know early how long setup takes, and wants to be told how sure any promised savings really are.
stated_up_front: I have about fifteen minutes today. Saint Ardent hospital bills are piling up and a collector wrote to me, and I think we might qualify for charity care. Can you check, and tell me what you need from me?

portals.mine: Cedar Valley Credit Union online banking

facts.truth: Nadia (50), husband Joseph (52), son Karim (17), and Nadia's father Elias (81), who lives in the back apartment and files his own taxes.
The tax preparer's summary lists Nadia, Joseph and Karim. Elias is not listed because he files his own return.
Part-time bookkeeping, $1,850 gross a month, so $5,550 for the three months.
$3,900 gross a month at an HVAC company, so $11,700 for the three months, plus $1,200 in unemployment in July after a two-week layoff.
About $620 a month from his grocery-store job. He is a teenager, so it is not counted.

facts.about: Non-payroll deposits in the joint account that should not count
facts.truth: $1,480 tax refund, a $500 gift from Nadia's sister, a $2,000 transfer from savings, a $214 mileage reimbursement from Joseph's employer, and Elias's Social Security of $1,640 a month deposited to help with groceries.

Nadia's ER visit in June ($4,180) and her spinal injection in July ($2,960), plus Karim's wrist ER visit in August ($1,725). Also an already-approved account for Joseph's colonoscopy, an eyelid-lift consult Nadia had last spring, a Lakeshore Emergency Physicians bill, and a 2025 sleep study for Karim that was paid in full.
The agency wrote about the June ER visit and says it will report to the credit bureaus after 30 October.
An email from a company offering to 'reduce your hospital bills' for 30% of the savings, and a 'FINAL NOTICE' asking for a card number. She has not answered either.
About fifteen minutes per sitting. She uses large text and loses her place if a page logs her out.

unknowns: How many days she has to apply on each account, or when each one started counting.
Whether the hospital counts her father or Karim's wages in the household and income.
What the income limit for free care is under Saint Ardent's policy.
Whether the collector's 30 October date can be moved once an application is in.
Whether the Lakeshore Emergency Physicians bill is covered by the hospital's program.
